newsitem.title: CHINA: GM gets approval step for China project.
newsitem.headline: GM gets approval step for China project.

text.p: General Motors Corp has received approval for project registration from China's State Council (cabinet) for its giant joint venture auto project in Shanghai, a GM official said on Friday.
"The approval was given several days ago. This is an important step forward and we can proceed with the project," he said by telephone.
"But this is not the final approval. No-one knows when that will be given. The auto industry in China is tightly controlled by the government," he said, but declined to give further details.
GM plans to produce an upscale car in a $1 billion joint venture with Shanghai Automotive Industry Corp in a new plant in the Pudong New Area of Shanghai.
GM has said it wants to start production in the fourth quarter of 1998.

GM officials said in June that the original timetable for the project, which would allow GM to carve a niche in what many analysts see as the world's biggest potential car market, allowed for final approval to be given in June.

They said at that time that they still had the opportunity to meet their goal of starting production in the fourth quarter of 1998 and that they were negotiating with the Chinese side on the kind of car to be produced in Shanghai.
The model produced by the Shanghai factory would compete with models now imported into China, mainly from Japan.

Critics have said that the model to be produced at the plant is too large and will cater only to a limited market in China. They are sceptical about ambitious projections for car ownership in China, citing income levels and infrastructure problems.
